content.directions:
For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay based on the short passage given below. In your essay, you are to comment on the phenomenon described in the passage and suggest measures to address the issue. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

Some parents in China are overprotective of their children. They plan everything for their children, make all the decisions for them, and do not allow them to explore on their own in case they make mistakes or get hurt.

modelEssay.title: Overprotective Parents in China
modelEssay.content:
In contemporary China, a prevalent phenomenon is the overprotection of children by their parents. This overbearing care manifests in planning every detail of their children's lives, making decisions on their behalf, and restricting their autonomy for fear of mistakes or injury.

Such overprotection, while stemming from love and a desire to shield children from harm, can have detrimental effects. It hinders the development of independence and problem-solving skills, which are crucial for personal growth. Children who are not allowed to make decisions or face consequences may become overly reliant on their parents, lacking the resilience needed to navigate life's challenges. Moreover, this approach can stifle creativity and initiative, as children are not given the freedom to explore and learn from their own experiences.

To address this issue, parents should be encouraged to foster an environment that balances care with the promotion of autonomy. Allowing children to make age-appropriate decisions and learn from their mistakes can empower them to become self-reliant and resourceful individuals. Schools and communities can also play a role by providing guidance on how to raise independent children and by creating opportunities for children to engage in safe, supervised exploration.

transcript.text: Hi David, I haven't seen you in class for almost two weeks.

transcript.text: Hi Sarah, well it's a bit of a long story I'm afraid.

transcript.text: I got a throat infection last week and had to go to the hospital to get some antibiotics as I really wasn't getting any better.

transcript.text: Oh yeah, there have been so many viruses going around this winter.

transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 过去几周天气一直很糟糕。

transcript.text: And on the way back from the hospital I slipped on some ice and fell and then had to go to the hospital to get an x-ray because I basically thought I'd broken my wrist.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 而且在从医院回来的路上，我在冰上滑倒摔了一跤，然后不得不回医院拍X光，因为我基本上以为我手腕骨折了。

transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Oh that's too bad, how unfortunate.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 哦，那太糟了，真不幸。

transcript.text: To make things worse, I managed to fall right in front of four girls from the ninth grade, so I was utterly humiliated.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 更糟的是，我居然在四个九年级女生面前摔倒了，所以我彻底丢脸了。

transcript.text: Plus the laptop in my bag was broken too.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 而且我包里的笔记本电脑也坏了。

transcript.text: Now what a complete catastrophe.

transcript.translation: 这真是个彻底的灾难。

transcript.translation: 笔记本电脑还在保修期内吗？

transcript.translation: 如果是的话，你可以轻松地把它寄回制造商，他们肯定会免费寄一台全新的给你。

transcript.text: The warranty ran out three days before I broke it and all my essays are in there and I need to hand them in before we break for the Christmas holidays.

transcript.translation: 保修期在我弄坏它前三天就到期了，而且我所有的文章都在里面，我需要在圣诞假期前交上去。

transcript.text: Listen, I have the number of a really good affordable computer repair shop at home.

transcript.translation: 我爸爸以前用过这个人，他能创造奇迹。

transcript.text: Conversation two.
transcript.translation: 对话二。

transcript.text: Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 欢迎收听本周的《图书漫谈》节目。

transcript.text: With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 今天与我一同做客的是历史学家海蒂·布朗，她撰写了五本备受好评的军事历史著作。

transcript.text: Thanks for having me, John.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 谢谢邀请我，约翰。

transcript.text: I'm so excited to talk about my latest book, which was published last month.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我非常兴奋能谈论我的新书，它上个月出版。

transcript.text: So, this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre, and thus a bit of a departure for you.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 所以，这本书是一部小说，你首次尝试这种体裁，因此对你来说有点偏离常规。

transcript.text: I'd say it's a major departure, as it's not just a work of fiction.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我得说这是一个重大转变，因为它不仅仅是一部虚构作品。

transcript.text: It's set 200 years in the future.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 它设定在200年后。

transcript.text: Right, so how did that happen?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那么，这是怎么发生的？

transcript.text: You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries, and now you're speculating about the future.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你花了三十年时间书写过去，专注于18和19世纪，而现在你在推测未来。

transcript.text: Well, after years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，经过多年研究士兵并记录他们在战斗中的生活，我开始好奇他们生活的其他方面，尤其是他们的个人生活。

transcript.text: I can see that.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我能理解。

transcript.text: Your novel is about soldiers, but it focuses on their relationships, especially the bonds between sons and mothers and men and their wives.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你的小说是关于士兵的，但它聚焦于他们的关系，尤其是儿子与母亲、男人与妻子之间的纽带。

transcript.text: Yes, that focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，这种聚焦是在我仍然打算写另一本历史书时产生的。

transcript.text: I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我开始研究士兵的真实个人生活，研究他们写回家的信件。

transcript.text: So, how did that history book become a novel?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那么，那本历史书是怎么变成小说的？

transcript.text: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete, so I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，我意识到历史记录不完整，所以我要么留下很多空白，要么做出比历史学家应有的更多的假设。

transcript.text: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但为什么写一部设定在未来的小说，而你的资历非常适合写历史小说呢？

transcript.text: As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 作为历史学家，你写的任何历史小说都会有很大的可信度。

transcript.text: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我觉得在过去题材上工作太受限制，就像我写的东西需要是事实而不是虚构。

transcript.text: But writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但书写未来给了我更多的自由去想象、去创造。

transcript.text: Well, having read your book, I'm glad you made that choice to move into fiction.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，读了你的书后，我很高兴你做出了转向虚构作品的选择。

transcript.text: Whether it's in the hands of animated polar bears or Santa Claus, there's one thing you'll find in nearly all ads for Coca-Cola, the characteristic glass bottle.
transcript.translation: 无论是动画北极熊还是圣诞老人手中，你在几乎所有可口可乐广告中都能找到一样东西，那就是标志性的玻璃瓶。

transcript.text: Most Americans don't drink soda out of the glass bottles seen in Coke's ads anymore.
transcript.translation: 大多数美国人不再从可口可乐广告中看到的玻璃瓶里喝苏打水了。

transcript.text: But this week, the company is celebrating a century of the bottle that's been sold in more than 200 countries.
transcript.translation: 但本周，该公司正在庆祝这款瓶子的一百年，它已在200多个国家销售。

transcript.text: Flashback to 1915, when a bottle of Coca-Cola cost just a nickel.
transcript.translation: 回到1915年，当时一瓶可口可乐只需5分钱。

transcript.text: As the soft drink gained in popularity, it faced a growing number of competitors, counterfeits even trying to copy Coke's logo.
transcript.translation: 随着这款软饮料的普及，它面临着越来越多的竞争对手，甚至仿冒品试图复制可口可乐的标志。

transcript.text: So according to Coca-Cola historian Ted Ryan, the company decided to come up with packaging that couldn't be duplicated.
transcript.translation: 因此，据可口可乐历史学家泰德·瑞安称，公司决定设计一种无法被复制的包装。

transcript.text: A product request was sent to eight different glass makers.
transcript.translation: 一份产品要求被发送给了八家不同的玻璃制造商。

transcript.text: Workers at the Root Glass Company got the request and began flipping through the encyclopedia at the local library, landing on cocoa seed.
transcript.translation: 鲁特玻璃公司的工人们收到了要求，并开始在当地图书馆翻阅百科全书，最终选中了可可种子。

transcript.text: Though cocoa seed is not an ingredient of the soda, they designed their bottle based on the seed's shape and large middle.
transcript.translation: 尽管可可种子不是这种苏打水的成分，但他们根据种子的形状和宽大的中间部分设计了瓶子。

transcript.text: It won over Coke executives in Atlanta and would go on to receive its own trademark, spur collections and earn Coca-Cola an iconic image that made it part of American culture for a century.
transcript.translation: 它赢得了亚特兰大可口可乐高管的青睐，并随后获得了自己的商标，刺激了收藏热，并为可口可乐赢得了一个标志性形象，使其成为美国文化的一部分长达一个世纪。

transcript.text: It was 100 years ago this week that the bottle earned a patent.
transcript.translation: 正是在100年前的本周，这款瓶子获得了专利。

transcript.text: By World War II, Coke bottle sales had ballooned into billions.
transcript.translation: 到第二次世界大战时，可口可乐瓶的销售额已膨胀至数十亿。

transcript.text: Americans mostly consume Coke out of aluminum or plastic today, but the glass bottle remains a symbol of America that's readily recognized around the world.
transcript.translation: 今天，美国人大多从铝罐或塑料瓶中饮用可口可乐，但玻璃瓶仍然是美国的象征，在全球范围内易于识别。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 篇章2。

transcript.text: Research shows that a few moments of conversation with a stranger creates a measurable improvement in mood, but most of us are reluctant to start these conversations because we presume the opposite.
transcript.translation: 研究表明，与陌生人片刻的交谈能显著改善情绪，但我们大多数人不愿开始这样的交谈，因为我们认为情况相反。

transcript.text: In an experiment, commuters who talked to nearby strangers found their commute more enjoyable than those who didn't.
transcript.translation: 在一项实验中，与附近陌生人交谈的通勤者发现他们的通勤比不交谈的人更愉快。

transcript.text: They were asked to predict whether they'd enjoy the commute more if they conversed with other people.
transcript.translation: 他们被要求预测，如果与其他人交谈，是否会更享受通勤。

transcript.text: Intriguingly, most expected the more solitary experience to be more pleasurable.
transcript.translation: 有趣的是，大多数人预期更孤独的经历会更愉快。

transcript.text: Why is this?
transcript.translation: 为什么会这样？

transcript.text: Social anxiety appears to be the problem.
transcript.translation: 社交焦虑似乎是问题所在。

transcript.text: People's reluctance to start conversations with nearby strangers comes partly from underestimating others' interest in connecting.
transcript.translation: 人们不愿与附近陌生人开始交谈，部分原因是低估了他人建立联系的兴趣。

transcript.text: The sad thing is that people presume that a nearby stranger doesn't want to converse and don't start a conversation.
transcript.translation: 可悲的是，人们认为附近陌生人不想交谈，从而不开始对话。

transcript.text: Only those who forced themselves to chat because it was required by the experiment found out what a pleasant experience it could be.
transcript.translation: 只有那些因实验要求而强迫自己交谈的人，才发现这可能是多么愉快的经历。

transcript.text: Human beings are social animals.
transcript.translation: 人类是社会性动物。

transcript.text: Those who misunderstand the impact of social interactions may not.
transcript.translation: 那些误解社交互动影响的人可能不会。

transcript.text: In some contexts, be social enough for their own well-being.
transcript.translation: 在某些情况下，为了自身福祉，要足够社交。

transcript.text: You should be chatting with the strangers you encounter.
transcript.translation: 你应该与遇到的陌生人聊天。

transcript.text: You may occasionally have a negative encounter that might stick in your memory.
transcript.translation: 你可能偶尔会有负面遭遇，这可能会留在记忆中。

transcript.text: This is because the human brain is biased to dwell on negative events.
transcript.translation: 这是因为人脑倾向于纠结于负面事件。

transcript.text: But starting conversations with strangers is still well worth the risk of rejection.
transcript.translation: 但与陌生人开始交谈，仍然值得冒被拒绝的风险。

transcript.text: It may surprise you that conversing with strangers will make them happier too.
transcript.translation: 可能会让你惊讶的是，与陌生人交谈也会让他们更快乐。

transcript.text: The pleasure of connection seems contagious.
transcript.translation: 连接的愉悦似乎是具有感染力的。

transcript.text: People who are talked to have equally positive experiences as those who initiate a conversation.
transcript.translation: 被交谈的人与发起交谈的人有同样积极的经历。

transcript.text: Recording 1.
transcript.translation: 录音1。

transcript.text: The Caribbean islands are divided into two worlds.
transcript.translation: 加勒比群岛被划分为两个世界。

transcript.text: A rich one and a poor one.
transcript.translation: 一个是富裕的世界，另一个是贫困的世界。

transcript.text: This tropical region's economy is based mainly on farming.
transcript.translation: 这个热带地区的经济主要基于农业。

transcript.text: Farmers are of two types.
transcript.translation: 农民分为两种类型。

transcript.text: One is the plantation owner who may have hundreds of thousands of acres.
transcript.translation: 一种是种植园主，可能拥有数十万英亩的土地。

transcript.text: In contrast, the small cultivator is working only a few acres of land.
transcript.translation: 相比之下，小种植者只耕种几英亩的土地。

transcript.text: Most visitors to the Caribbean are rich.
transcript.translation: 大多数前往加勒比地区的游客都很富有。

transcript.text: Like the plantation owner, they do not realize or do not want to realize that many farm families barely manage to get by on what they grow.
transcript.translation: 像种植园主一样，他们没有意识到或不愿意意识到，许多农家家庭仅靠种植的东西勉强维持生计。

transcript.text: The Caribbean produces many things.
transcript.translation: 加勒比地区生产许多产品。

transcript.text: Sugar is the main product.
transcript.translation: 糖是主要产品。

transcript.text: Other export crops are tobacco, coffee, bananas, spices, and citrus fruits, such as orange, lemon, or grapefruit.
transcript.translation: 其他出口作物包括烟草、咖啡、香蕉、香料和柑橘类水果，如橙子、柠檬或葡萄柚。

transcript.text: From the West Indies also come oil, mineral pitch, and many forest products.
transcript.translation: 西印度群岛也出口石油、矿物沥青和许多林产品。

transcript.text: Jamaica's aluminum ore supplies are the world's largest.
transcript.translation: 牙买加的铝土矿储量是世界上最大的。

transcript.text: Oil comes from Trinidad, Aruba, and Caraco.
transcript.translation: 石油来自特立尼达、阿鲁巴和库拉索。

transcript.text: But for many of the smaller islands, sugar is the only export.
transcript.translation: 但对于许多较小的岛屿来说，糖是唯一的出口产品。

transcript.text: Rum, a strong alcoholic drink, which is distilled from sugar cane, is also an export.
transcript.translation: 朗姆酒，一种用甘蔗蒸馏制成的烈性酒精饮料，也是一种出口产品。

transcript.text: The world's best rum comes from this area.
transcript.translation: 世界上最好的朗姆酒来自这个地区。

transcript.text: Local kinds vary, from the light rums of Puerto Rico to the heavier, darker rums of Barbados and Jamaica.
transcript.translation: 当地品种各异，从波多黎各的淡朗姆酒到巴巴多斯和牙买加更浓烈、更暗色的朗姆酒。

transcript.text: American tourists enjoy stocking up on inexpensive, high-quality Caribbean rum while they are on vacation.
transcript.translation: 美国游客在度假时喜欢大量购买物美价廉的加勒比朗姆酒。

transcript.text: In Caraco, the well-known liquor of that name is made from the thick outer skin of a native orange.
transcript.translation: 在库拉索，那种著名的利口酒是用当地橙子的厚外皮制成的。

transcript.text: Ever since America's colonial days, the Caribbean islands have been favorite places to visit.
transcript.translation: 自美国殖民时代以来，加勒比群岛一直是人们喜爱的旅游目的地。

transcript.text: Since World War II, tourism has increased rapidly.
transcript.translation: 自第二次世界大战以来，旅游业迅速增长。

transcript.text: Because great numbers of people go there, the islanders have built elaborate resorts, developed harbors and airfields, improved beaches, and have expanded sea and air routes.
transcript.translation: 由于大量的人前往那里，岛民们建造了精致的度假胜地，开发了港口和机场，改善了海滩，并扩展了海空航线。

transcript.text: Everything is at the resort.
transcript.translation: 度假胜地里应有尽有。

transcript.text: Hotel, beach, shopping, and recreation.
transcript.translation: 酒店、海滩、购物和娱乐。

transcript.text: The vacationer never has any reason to explore the island.
transcript.translation: 度假者从没有任何理由去探索岛屿。

transcript.text: As in most places, those who have money live well indeed.
transcript.translation: 像在大多数地方一样，有钱的人确实生活得很好。

transcript.text: Those who don't have money live at various levels of poverty.
transcript.translation: 没有钱的人生活在不同程度的贫困中。

transcript.text: But here, the poor greatly outnumber the wealthy.
transcript.translation: 但在这里，穷人远远多于富人。

transcript.text: A visitor will find rich people living in apartments or Spanish houses at the seaside or in the countryside.
transcript.translation: 游客会发现富人住在海边或乡村的公寓或西班牙式房屋中。

transcript.text: Their servants might include a cook, a maid, and a nurse for the children.
transcript.translation: 他们的仆人可能包括一名厨师、一名女佣和一名照顾孩子的保姆。

transcript.text: Most of the people live well below the poverty level.
transcript.translation: 大多数人的生活水平远低于贫困线。

transcript.text: In towns, they live crowded together in tiny houses.
transcript.translation: 在城镇，他们拥挤地住在狭小的房子里。

transcript.text: Islanders make the best they can of what they have.
transcript.translation: 岛民们充分利用他们所拥有的一切。

transcript.text: Their homes are quite shabby.
transcript.translation: 他们的家相当破旧。

transcript.text: Sadly, most tourists never see this side of the Caribbean.
transcript.translation: 可悲的是，大多数游客从未看到加勒比地区的这一面。

transcript.text: Recording 2.
transcript.translation: 录音2。

transcript.text: Talk to anyone who is a generation or two older, and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days.
transcript.translation: 与比你年长一两代的任何人交谈，他们很可能会评论说如今的孩子更娇惯。

transcript.text: No one wants to have or be around demanding, selfish, and spoiled children.
transcript.translation: 没有人想要或愿意与任性、自私、娇惯的孩子相处。

transcript.text: Those who get bad-tempered or silently brood when they're not given everything they want immediately.
transcript.translation: 那些当不能立即得到想要的一切时就脾气暴躁或默默生闷气的孩子。

transcript.text: Paradoxically, the parents of such children encourage this demanding behavior in the mistaken belief that by giving their children everything they can, their children will be happy.
transcript.translation: 矛盾的是，这些孩子的父母鼓励这种任性行为，错误地认为给予孩子一切就能使他们快乐。

transcript.text: In the short term, perhaps they are right.
transcript.translation: 短期来看，或许他们是对的。

transcript.text: But in the longer term, such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied, and resentful of the parents who tried so hard to please them.
transcript.translation: 但从长远来看，这些孩子最终会变得孤独、依赖、长期不满，并对那些努力取悦他们的父母心怀怨恨。

transcript.text: Undoubtedly, parents want to raise happy children who are confident, capable, and likable rather than spoiled and miserable.
transcript.translation: 毫无疑问，父母希望培养出自信、能干、讨人喜欢的孩子，而不是娇惯且不幸的孩子。

transcript.text: One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets, and the like.
transcript.translation: 阻碍这一点的一个因素是，父母无法或没有花足够多的时间陪伴孩子，并用玩具、游戏、小玩意等来弥补这种缺失。

transcript.text: Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention.
transcript.translation: 孩子们需要的不是物质的东西，而是父母专注的关注。

transcript.text: The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time.
transcript.translation: 一起度过的时间的数量不如这段时间的内容重要。

transcript.text: Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have.
transcript.translation: 父母不应立即满足孩子的愿望，而应帮助他们制定计划，通过努力获得想要的东西。

transcript.text: This teaches them to value their effort as well as what it achieves.
transcript.translation: 这教会他们珍视自己的努力及其成果。

transcript.text: Allow them to enjoy anticipation.
transcript.translation: 让他们享受期待的乐趣。

transcript.text: Numerous psychological studies have demonstrated that children who learn to wait for things they desire are more likely to succeed in a number of ways later in life.
transcript.translation: 众多心理学研究表明，学会等待想要的东西的孩子，更可能在未来的生活中取得多方面的成功。

transcript.text: One famous experiment in the 1960s involved three to six-year-old children.
transcript.translation: 20世纪60年代一个著名的实验涉及3至6岁的儿童。

transcript.text: They were given a choice between receiving a small reward, such as a cookie, immediately, or if they waited 15 minutes, they could have two.
transcript.translation: 他们可以选择立即获得一个小奖励，如一块饼干，或者等待15分钟获得两块。

transcript.text: Follow-up studies have found that those who chose to delay satisfaction are now more academically successful, have greater self-worth, and even tend to be healthier.
transcript.translation: 后续研究发现，那些选择延迟满足的孩子，现在学业上更成功，自我价值感更强，甚至更健康。

transcript.text: If they fail, children should be encouraged to keep trying rather than to give up if they really want the desired result.
transcript.translation: 如果他们失败了，应该鼓励孩子们继续努力，而不是放弃，如果他们真正想要达到预期结果的话。

transcript.text: This teaches them how to handle and recover from disappointment, which is associated with greater success and satisfaction academically, financially, and in personal relationships.
transcript.translation: 这教会他们如何应对和从失望中恢复，这与学业、财务和人际关系上更大的成功和满足感相关。

transcript.text: And lastly, parents should encourage their children to look at life from other points of view as well as their own.
transcript.translation: 最后，父母应该鼓励孩子从他人视角以及自己的视角看待生活。

transcript.text: This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others, qualities sure to take them a long way in life.
transcript.translation: 这教会他们理解和同情他人，这些品质必将使他们受益终生。

transcript.text: Recording 3.

transcript.text: It's not hard to mess up an interview.
transcript.translation: 搞砸一场面试并不难。

transcript.text: Most people feel nervous sitting across from a hiring manager, answering questions that effectively open themselves up for judgment.
transcript.translation: 大多数人坐在招聘经理对面，回答那些实际上让自己接受评判的问题时，都会感到紧张。

transcript.text: And your chances of being more carefully considered for the job can quickly go downhill just by saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
transcript.translation: 而你被更认真考虑获得这份工作的机会，可能会因为说错话而迅速下降。

transcript.text: The most obvious thing not to do is complain.
transcript.translation: 最明显不要做的事情就是抱怨。

transcript.text: Employers want to hire positive people.
transcript.translation: 雇主希望雇佣积极的人。

transcript.text: Talking about a previous job negatively raises concerns that you might be difficult to manage, or you might be someone that blames management for your own poor performance.
transcript.translation: 负面谈论上一份工作会引发担忧，认为你可能难以管理，或者你可能是那种把自己的糟糕表现归咎于管理层的人。

transcript.text: Don't say that you've moved around in jobs because you haven't found the right fit or feel that you were not challenged enough.
transcript.translation: 不要说你频繁换工作是因为没有找到合适的职位，或者觉得挑战不够。

transcript.text: Statements like these will make you sound aimless and lost.
transcript.translation: 这样的话会让你听起来没有目标感，迷失方向。

transcript.text: An interviewer may well think, why would this role be any different for you?
transcript.translation: 面试官很可能会想，这个职位对你来说会有什么不同呢？

transcript.text: You will probably leave here in six months.
transcript.translation: 你很可能六个月后就会离开这里。

transcript.text: It also begs the question of what type of relationship you had with your manager.
transcript.translation: 这也引出了一个问题，你与经理的关系是怎样的。

transcript.text: It doesn't sound like you had open communication with him or her.
transcript.translation: 听起来你与他或她没有开放的沟通。

transcript.text: Managers usually love people who can self-sustain and enable growth through taking initiative, who are strong at following through their work, and who bring ideas and solutions to the table.
transcript.translation: 经理通常喜欢那些能够自我维持、通过主动性促进成长、擅长跟进工作、并能提出想法和解决方案的人。

transcript.text: If you were in a management or leadership position, when discussing your current role, never take all the credit for accomplishments or achievements.
transcript.translation: 如果你处于管理或领导职位，在讨论你当前角色时，不要独揽所有成就或功绩。

transcript.text: Emphasize your team and how through their talents, your vision was realized.
transcript.translation: 强调你的团队，以及通过他们的才能如何实现了你的愿景。

transcript.text: Most successful leaders know that they are only as good as their team.
transcript.translation: 大多数成功的领导者知道，他们和团队一样优秀。

transcript.text: And acknowledging this in an interview will go a long way towards suggesting that you might be the right person for the position you are applying for.
transcript.translation: 在面试中承认这一点，将大大有助于表明你可能是所申请职位的合适人选。

transcript.text: Lastly, have a good idea of what your role will be and try and convey the idea that you're flexible.
transcript.translation: 最后，清楚了解你的角色将是什么，并努力传达你具有灵活性。

transcript.text: Asking what your role will be suggests you will limit yourself purely to what is expected of you.
transcript.translation: 询问你的角色将是什么，暗示你将把自己限制在对你的期望之内。

transcript.text: In reality, your role is whatever you make of it.
transcript.translation: 实际上，你的角色取决于你如何创造它。

transcript.text: This is especially true in small companies, where the ability to adapt and take on new responsibilities is highly valued.
transcript.translation: 这在小公司尤其如此，在那里适应能力和承担新职责的能力受到高度重视。

transcript.text: And this is equally important if you're just starting out.
transcript.translation: 如果你刚开始工作，这同样重要。

transcript.text: Entry-level interviewees would do well to demonstrate a broad set of skills in most interviews.
transcript.translation: 初级面试者最好在大多数面试中展示广泛的技能。

transcript.text: It's important to have a wide skill set.
transcript.translation: 拥有广泛的技能集很重要。

transcript.text: As many startups and small companies are moving really fast, employers are looking for candidates that are intelligent and can quickly adapt and excel in a growing company.
transcript.translation: 由于许多初创公司和小型公司发展迅速，雇主正在寻找那些聪明、能够快速适应并在成长中的公司里表现出色的候选人。

paragraphs.text: If you think life is wonderful and expect it to stay that way, then you may have a good chance of living to a ripe old age, at least that is what the findings of a new study suggest. That study found that participants who reported the highest levels of optimism were far more likely to live to age 85 or __26__. This was compared to those participants who reported the lowest levels of optimism. It is __27__ that the findings held even after the researchers considered factors that could __28__ the link, including whether participants had health conditions, such as heart disease or cancer, or whether they experienced depression.
paragraphs.translation: 如果你认为生活是美好的并期望它保持这样，那么你可能有很好的机会活到高龄，至少一项新研究的发现表明如此。该研究发现，报告最高乐观水平的参与者活到85岁或更长寿命的可能性远高于那些报告最低乐观水平的参与者。值得注意的是，在研究人员考虑了可能影响这一联系的因素后，这些发现依然成立，包括参与者是否有健康问题，如心脏病或癌症，或者他们是否经历过抑郁症。

paragraphs.text: The results add to a growing body of evidence that certain psychological factors may predict a longer life __29__. For example, previous studies have found that more optimistic people have a lower risk of developing chronic diseases, and a lower risk of __30__ death. However, the new study appears to be the first to __31__ look at the relationship between optimism and longevity. The researchers __32__ that the link found in the new study was not as strong when they factored in the effects of certain health behaviors, including exercise levels, sleep habits and diet. This suggests that these behaviors may, at least in part, explain the link. In other words, optimism may __33__ good habits that bolster health.
paragraphs.translation: 这些结果为日益增长的证据库增添了新内容，表明某些心理因素可能预测更长寿命的相关性。例如，以往研究发现，更乐观的人患慢性疾病的风险较低，早逝的风险也较低。然而，这项新研究似乎是第一个专门探讨乐观与长寿关系的研究。研究人员承认，当他们考虑某些健康行为的影响时，包括运动水平、睡眠习惯和饮食，新研究中发现的联系并不那么强。这表明这些行为可能至少部分地解释了这一联系。换句话说，乐观可能培养出有益健康的习惯。

paragraphs.text: It is also important to note that the study found only a __34__, as researchers did not prove for certain that optimism leads to a longer life. However, if the findings are true, they suggest that optimism could serve as a psychological __35__ that promotes health and a longer life.
paragraphs.translation: 同样重要的是要注意，该研究仅发现了一种可能性，因为研究人员并未确切证明乐观会导致更长寿命。然而，如果这些发现属实，它们表明乐观可能作为一种心理特质促进健康和长寿。

空格在"may predict a longer life __"，需要名词与 life 构成固定搭配。life span（寿命、生命跨度）是固定搭配，"a longer life span"即"更长的寿命"，与全文"乐观预示更长寿命"主旨一致，故选 L span。correlation（相关性）此处搭配不当，且它更适合第34空"found only a correlation"，排除。

questionGroups.title: No one in fashion is surprised that Burberry burnt £28 million of stock

material.title: No one in fashion is surprised that Burberry burnt £28 million of stock

paragraphs.text: Last week, Burberry's annual report revealed that £28.6 million worth of stock was burnt last year. The news has left investors and consumers outraged but comes as little surprise to those in the fashion industry.
paragraphs.translation: 上周，Burberry的年报显示，去年有价值2860万英镑的库存被焚烧。这一消息让投资者和消费者感到愤怒，但对时尚行业的人来说却并不意外。

paragraphs.text: The practice of destroying unsold stock, and even rolls of unused fabric, is commonplace for luxury labels. Becoming too widely available at a cheaper price through discount stores discourages full-price sales. Sending products for recycling leaves them vulnerable to being stolen and sold on the black market. Jasmine Bina, CEO of brand strategy agency Concept Bureau explains, "Typically, luxury brands rally around exclusivity to protect their business interests, namely intellectual property and preservation of brand equity (资产)." She stated she had heard rumors of stock burning but not specific cases until this week.
paragraphs.translation: 销毁未售出库存，甚至未使用的布料卷，对于奢侈品牌来说是司空见惯的做法。通过折扣店以更便宜的价格变得过于普及会阻碍全价销售。将产品送去回收会使它们容易被盗并在黑市上出售。品牌战略机构Concept Bureau的首席执行官Jasmine Bina解释说：“通常，奢侈品牌围绕排他性来保护其商业利益，即知识产权和品牌资产的维护。”她表示，她曾听到过焚烧库存的传言，但直到本周才有具体案例。

paragraphs.text: Another reason for the commonplace practice is a financial incentive for brands exporting goods to America. United States Customs states that if imported merchandise is unused and destroyed under their supervision, 99% of the duties, taxes or fees paid on the merchandise may be recovered. It is incredibly difficult to calculate how much dead stock currently goes to waste. While there are incentives to do it, there's no legal obligation to report it.
paragraphs.translation: 这种常见做法的另一个原因是品牌向美国出口商品的财务激励。美国海关规定，如果进口商品未使用且在其监督下销毁，商品上支付的99%的关税、税费或费用可以收回。目前很难计算有多少废弃库存被浪费。虽然有激励这样做，但没有法律义务报告。

paragraphs.text: A source, who chose to remain anonymous, shared her experience working in a Burberry store in New York in October 2016. "My job was to toss items in boxes so they could be sent to be burned. It was killing me inside because all that leather and fur went to waste and animals had died for nothing. I couldn't stay there any longer, their business practices threw me off the roof." In May this year, Burberry announced it was taking fur out of its catwalk shows and reviewing its use elsewhere in the business. "Even though we asked the management, they refused to give us detailed answers as to why they would do this with their collection," continued the source, who left her role within two weeks. She has since worked with another high-profile, luxury label.
paragraphs.translation: 一位选择匿名的消息人士分享了她2016年10月在纽约一家Burberry店铺工作的经历。“我的工作是把物品扔进盒子里，以便送去焚烧。这让我内心很痛苦，因为所有那些皮革和毛皮都浪费了，动物们白白死了。我再也待不下去了，他们的商业做法让我崩溃。”今年5月，Burberry宣布将从其时装秀中剔除毛皮，并审查其在其他业务中的使用。“即使我们问了管理层，他们也拒绝给出详细答案，说明他们为什么会对他们的系列这样做，”这位消息人士继续说道，她在两周内离开了职位。此后，她曾为另一家知名奢侈品牌工作。

paragraphs.text: In an online forum post, which asked if it's true that Louis Vuitton burned its bags, Ahmed Bouchfaa, who claimed to work for Louis Vuitton, responded that the brand holds sales of old stock for staff members twice a year. Items which have still not sold after several sales are destroyed. "Louis Vuitton doesn't have public sales. They either sell a product at a given price or discontinue it. This is to make sure that everybody pays the same price for an item," he says. He goes on to disclose the strict guidelines around the employee sales: "You may buy gifts for someone, but they track each item, and if your gift ends up online they know who to ask." One investor commenting on the Burberry figures was reportedly outraged that the unsold goods were not even offered to investors before they were destroyed.
paragraphs.translation: 在一个在线论坛帖子中，有人问Louis Vuitton焚烧其手袋是否属实，自称在Louis Vuitton工作的Ahmed Bouchfaa回应说，该品牌每年为员工举办两次旧库存销售。经过多次销售仍未售出的商品会被销毁。“Louis Vuitton没有公开销售。他们要么以给定价格出售产品，要么停产。这是为了确保每个人为一件物品支付相同的价格，”他说。他接着披露了关于员工销售的严格指南：“你可以为别人买礼物，但他们会追踪每件物品，如果你的礼物最终出现在网上，他们知道该问谁。”一位投资者评论Burberry的数据时，据报道对未售出商品在销毁前甚至没有提供给投资者感到愤怒。

paragraphs.text: Richemont, who owns several luxury brands, hit the headlines in May for taking back £437 million of watches for destruction in the last two years to avoid marked-down prices. It's not just luxury brands either. In October last year, a Danish TV show exposed H&M for burning 12 tonnes of unsold clothing since 2013. In a statement, the high street retailer defended itself by saying that the burnt clothing had failed safety tests: "The products to which the media are referring have been tested in external laboratories. The test results show that one of the products is mold infested and the other product contains levels of lead that are too high. Those products have rightly been stopped in accordance with our safety routines." In March, a report revealed that H&M was struggling with $4.3 billion worth of unsold stock. The brand told The New York Times that the plan was to reduce prices to move the stock, arguably encouraging consumers to buy and throw away with little thought.
paragraphs.translation: 拥有多个奢侈品牌的Richemont在5月登上头条，因为过去两年收回价值4.37亿英镑的手表进行销毁，以避免降价。不仅仅是奢侈品牌。去年10月，一家丹麦电视节目揭露H&M自2013年以来焚烧了12吨未售出的服装。在一份声明中，这家高街零售商为自己辩护，称焚烧的服装未通过安全测试：“媒体所指的产品已在外部实验室进行了测试。测试结果显示，其中一种产品发霉，另一种产品铅含量过高。这些产品已根据我们的安全程序被正确停止。”3月，一份报告显示，H&M正挣扎于价值43亿美元的未售出库存。该品牌告诉《纽约时报》，计划是降低价格以清理库存，这可以说鼓励消费者不假思索地购买和丢弃。

paragraphs.text: Over-production is perhaps the biggest concern for Burberry. While there has been much outrage at the elitist connotation of burning goods rather than making them affordable, executives at the British fashion house are no doubt struggling to defend how they miscalculated production? The waste has been put down to burning old cosmetic stock to make way for their new beauty range. However, while the value of destroyed stock is up from £26.9 million last year, it's an even more significant increase from 2016's figure of £18.8 million, highlighting that this is an ongoing issue.
paragraphs.translation: 生产过剩或许是Burberry最大的担忧。尽管焚烧商品而不是让其变得负担得起引发了关于精英主义内涵的愤怒，这家英国时装公司的高管们无疑在努力为他们的生产误判辩护？这种浪费被归因于焚烧旧的化妆品库存，以为他们的新美容系列让路。然而，尽管销毁库存的价值从去年的2690万英镑上升，但从2016年的1880万英镑数字来看，这是一个更显著的增长，突显这是一个持续存在的问题。

paragraphs.text: In September 2016, Burberry switched to a "see now, buy now" catwalk show format. The move was a switch to leverage on the coverage of their fashion week show to make stock available immediately to consumers. This is opposed to the traditional format of presenting to the industry, taking orders for production and becoming available in six months' time. While Burberry announced "record-breaking" online reach and engagement, there has been little evidence to suggest that the strategy has had a significant effect on sales, particularly as the hype (炒作) slows across the season. In February they made adjustments to the format, dropping some catwalk items immediately and promising that others would launch in the coming months.
paragraphs.translation: 2016年9月，Burberry转向“即看即买”的时装秀形式。这一举措是为了利用时装秀的媒体报道，让库存立即向消费者提供。这与向行业展示、接受生产订单并在六个月后上市的传统形式相反。虽然Burberry宣布了“破纪录”的在线覆盖和参与度，但几乎没有证据表明该策略对销售有显著影响，特别是随着季节变化炒作减退。2月，他们调整了形式，立即推出一些时装秀商品，并承诺其他商品将在未来几个月内上市。

paragraphs.text: In a statement, Burberry denied that switching to "see now, buy now" has had an impact on waste. A Burberry spokesperson further said, "On the occasions when disposal of products is necessary, we do so in a responsible manner. We are always seeking ways to reduce and revalue our waste. This is a core part of our strategy and we have forged partnerships and committed support to innovative organizations to help reach this goal."
paragraphs.translation: 在一份声明中，Burberry否认转向“即看即买”对浪费产生了影响。Burberry发言人进一步表示：“在需要处理产品的情况下，我们以负责任的方式进行。我们一直在寻找减少和重新评估我们浪费的方法。这是我们战略的核心部分，我们已与创新组织建立伙伴关系并承诺支持，以帮助实现这一目标。”

paragraphs.text: One such partnership is with Elvis & Kresse, an accessories brand working with reclaimed materials. Co-founder Kresse Wesling said, "Late last year we launched an ambitious five-year partnership with the Burberry Foundation. The main aim of this is to scale our leather rescue project, starting with off-cuts from the production of Burberry leather goods. We are working tirelessly to expand our solutions and would love to welcome anyone to our workshop to come and see what we are doing." At the moment, the partnership only addresses waste at the production stage and not unsold goods.
paragraphs.translation: 其中一个合作伙伴是与使用回收材料的配饰品牌Elvis & Kresse的合作。联合创始人Kresse Wesling说：“去年年底，我们与Burberry基金会启动了一项雄心勃勃的五年合作。主要目标是扩大我们的皮革拯救项目，从Burberry皮革制品生产中的边角料开始。我们正在不懈努力扩展我们的解决方案，并欢迎任何人到我们的工作室来看看我们正在做什么。”目前，该合作仅解决生产阶段的浪费，而不是未售出商品。

paragraphs.text: While these are honorable schemes, it makes it harder for Burberry to defend these latest figures. Fifteen years ago, Burberry was at crisis point as their signature check pattern was widely imitated by cheap, imitation brands. It deterred luxury consumers who found their expensive clothing more closely associated with working-class youth culture than a prestigious heritage fashion house. In the year 2004, at the height of over-exposure of the Burberry check, the brand's turnover was £715.5 million. Under Christopher Bailey as creative director they turned the brand around and this past year revenue hit £2.73 billion.
paragraphs.translation: 虽然这些都是值得称赞的计划，但这使得Burberry更难为这些最新数据辩护。十五年前，Burberry处于危机时刻，因为他们标志性的格子图案被廉价、仿冒品牌广泛模仿。这阻止了奢侈消费者，他们发现昂贵的服装更接近工人阶级青年文化，而不是一个享有盛誉的传承时装公司。2004年，在Burberry格子过度曝光的高峰时期，该品牌的营业额为7.155亿英镑。在Christopher Bailey担任创意总监期间，他们扭转了品牌局面，去年收入达到27.3亿英镑。

paragraphs.text: Bina believes that brands need to readdress their exclusivity tactic. "Exclusivity is starting to be challenged," she says. "I think that goes hand in hand with how luxury itself is being challenged. Access to fashion, and the brands who police it, are becoming less and less relevant. Things like health, enlightenment, and social and environmental responsibility are the new luxuries. These all come from within, not without. That's the challenge that traditional luxury brands will have to contend with in the mid- to long-term future."
paragraphs.translation: Bina认为品牌需要重新审视他们的排他性策略。“排他性开始受到挑战，”她说。“我认为这与奢侈本身如何受到挑战是相辅相成的。时尚的可及性，以及监管它的品牌，正变得越来越不相关。健康、启蒙、社会和环境责任等事物是新的奢侈。这些都来自内部，而不是外部。这是传统奢侈品牌在中长期未来必须应对的挑战。

questionGroups.directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.statementText: Burberry's executives are trying hard to attribute their practice of destroying old products to miscalculated production.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落G。段落G中提到'The waste has been put down to burning old cosmetic stock to make way for their new beauty range'（废物归因于焚烧旧化妆品库存以为新的美容系列腾出空间），这与陈述中的'attribute their practice of destroying old products to miscalculated production'（将销毁旧产品的做法归因于生产失误）相对应。关键词匹配：destroying old products对应burning old cosmetic stock, miscalculated production对应make way for their new beauty range。

questions.statementText: Selling products at a discount will do greater harm to luxury brands than destroying them.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落B。段落B中提到'Becoming too widely available at a cheaper price through discount stores discourages full-price sales'（通过折扣店以更便宜的价格过于广泛地可用会阻碍全价销售），这与陈述中的'Selling products at a discount will do greater harm to luxury brands than destroying them'（以折扣价销售产品对奢侈品牌的伤害大于销毁它们）相对应。关键词匹配：discount对应cheaper price, harm对应discourages full-price sales。

questions.statementText: Imitated Burberry products discouraged luxury consumers from buying its genuine products.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落K。段落K中提到'Burberry was at crisis point as their signature check pattern was widely imitated by cheap, imitation brands'（Burberry处于危机点，因为他们的标志性格子图案被廉价的仿冒品牌广泛模仿），这与陈述中的'Imitated Burberry products discouraged luxury consumers from buying its genuine products'（模仿的Burberry产品阻碍了奢侈消费者购买其真品）相对应。关键词匹配：imitated对应imitated by cheap imitation brands, discouraged对应crisis point。

questions.statementText: Staff members of a luxury brand may buy its old stock at cheaper prices, but they are not allowed to resell them.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落E。段落E中提到'Items which have still not sold after several sales are destroyed'（几轮销售后仍未售出的项目将被销毁）和'if your gift ends up online they know who to ask'（如果你的礼物最终在线出现，他们知道该问谁），这与陈述中的'Staff members of a luxury brand may buy its old stock at cheaper prices, but they are not allowed to resell them'（奢侈品牌的员工可以以较低的价格购买其旧库存，但不允许他们转售）相对应。关键词匹配：buy its old stock at cheaper prices对应sales of old stock, not allowed to resell them对应if your gift ends up online they know who to ask。

questions.statementText: In future traditional luxury brands will have to adapt their business strategies to the changing concepts of luxury.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落L。段落L中提到'brands need to readdress their exclusivity tactic'（品牌需要重新审视他们的独家策略）和'how luxury itself is being challenged'（奢侈品本身如何受到挑战），这与陈述中的'In future traditional luxury brands will have to adapt their business strategies to the changing concepts of luxury'（未来传统奢侈品牌将不得不适应奢侈品概念的变化以调整他们的商业策略）相对应。关键词匹配：adapt their business strategies对应readdress their exclusivity tactic, changing concepts of luxury对应how luxury itself is being challenged。

questions.statementText: One luxury brand employee quit her job because she simply couldn't bear to see the destruction of unsold products.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落D。段落D中提到'My job was to toss items in boxes so they could be sent to be burned... I couldn't stay there any longer, their business practices threw me off the roof'（我的工作是把物品扔进箱子里，这样它们就可以被送去焚烧...我不能再待在那里了，他们的商业实践让我感到绝望），这与陈述中的'One luxury brand employee quit her job because she simply couldn't bear to see the destruction of unsold products'（一名奢侈品牌员工辞职，因为她实在无法忍受看到未售出产品的销毁）相对应。关键词匹配：quit her job对应I couldn't stay there any longer, couldn't bear to see the destruction of unsold products对应their business practices threw me off the roof。

questions.statementText: Destroying old stock is a practice not just of luxury brands but of less prestigious fashion brands.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落F。段落F中提到'In October last year, a Danish TV show exposed H&M for burning 12 tonnes of unsold clothing since 2013'（去年10月，一个丹麦电视节目揭露了H&M自2013年以来焚烧了12吨未售出的服装），这与陈述中的'Destroying old stock is a practice not just of luxury brands but of less prestigious fashion brands'（销毁旧库存不仅是奢侈品牌的做法，也是不那么有声望的时尚品牌的做法）相对应。关键词匹配：Destroying old stock对应burning 12 tonnes of unsold clothing, less prestigious fashion brands对应H&M。

questions.statementText: Burberry is working with a partner to make full use of leather materials to reduce waste.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落J。段落J中提到'we launched an ambitious five-year partnership with the Burberry Foundation... to scale our leather rescue project, starting with off-cuts from the production of Burberry leather goods'（我们与Burberry基金会启动了一个雄心勃勃的五年合作伙伴关系...扩大我们的皮革救援项目，从Burberry皮具生产的余料开始），这与陈述中的'Burberry is working with a partner to make full use of leather materials to reduce waste'（Burberry正在与合作伙伴合作，充分利用皮革材料以减少浪费）相对应。关键词匹配：working with a partner对应launched an ambitious five-year partnership, make full use of leather materials对应scale our leather rescue project。

questions.statementText: Burberry's plan to destroy its unsold products worth millions of dollars aroused public indignation.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落A。段落A中提到'The news has left investors and consumers outraged'（这条新闻让投资者和消费者感到愤怒），这与陈述中的'Burberry's plan to destroy its unsold products worth millions of dollars aroused public indignation'（Burberry计划销毁价值数百万美元的未售出产品引起了公众愤慨）相对应。关键词匹配：aroused public indignation对应left investors and consumers outraged。

questions.statementText: Burberry's change of marketing strategy to make a product available as soon as consumers see it on the fashion show did not turn out to be as effective as expected.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落H。段落H中提到'there has been little evidence to suggest that the strategy has had a significant effect on sales'（几乎没有证据表明这种策略对销售有显著影响），这与陈述中的'Burberry's change of marketing strategy to make a product available as soon as consumers see it on the fashion show did not turn out to be as effective as expected'（Burberry改变营销策略，使产品在消费者看到时装秀后立即可用，结果并不像预期的那样有效）相对应。关键词匹配：change of marketing strategy对应switched to a 'see now, buy now' catwalk show format, did not turn out to be as effective as expected对应little evidence to suggest that the strategy has had a significant effect on sales。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Social media is absolutely everywhere. Billions of people use social media on a daily basis to create, share, and exchange ideas, messages, and information. Both individuals and businesses post regularly to engage and interact with people from around the world. It is a powerful communication medium that simultaneously provides immediate, frequent, permanent, and wide-reaching information across the globe.
paragraphs.translation: 社交媒体无处不在。数十亿人每天使用社交媒体来创建、分享和交换想法、信息和消息。个人和企业定期发布内容，以与世界各地的人们互动和交流。它是一种强大的通信媒介，能够同时提供即时、频繁、持久且覆盖全球的信息。

paragraphs.text: People post their lives on social media for the world to see. Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and countless other social channels provide a quick and simple way to glimpse into a job candidate's personal life—both the positive and negative sides of it. Social media screening is tempting to use as part of the hiring process, but should employers make use of it when researching a potential candidate's background?
paragraphs.translation: 人们在社交媒体上发布自己的生活供全世界观看。Facebook、Twitter、LinkedIn以及无数其他社交渠道提供了一种快速简便的方式，可以窥见求职者的个人生活——包括其积极和消极的一面。社交媒体筛查作为招聘过程的一部分很有吸引力，但雇主在调查潜在候选人的背景时是否应该使用它呢？

paragraphs.text: Incorporating the use of social media to screen job candidates is not an uncommon practice. A 2018 survey found that almost 70% of employers use social media to screen candidates before hiring them. But there are consequences and potential legal risks involved too. When done inappropriately, social media screening can be considered unethical or even illegal.
paragraphs.translation: 将社交媒体用于筛选求职者并非罕见做法。2018年的一项调查发现，近70%的雇主在雇用前使用社交媒体筛选候选人。但这也涉及后果和潜在的法律风险。如果不当进行，社交媒体筛查可能被视为不道德甚至非法。

paragraphs.text: Social media screening is essentially scrutinising a job candidate's private life. It can reveal information about protected characteristics like age, race, nationality, disability, gender, religion, etc. and that could bias a hiring decision. Pictures or comments on a private page that are taken out of context could ruin a perfectly good candidate's chances of getting hired. This process could potentially give an unfair advantage to one candidate over another. It creates an unequal playing field and potentially provides hiring managers with information that can impact their hiring decision in a negative way.
paragraphs.translation: 社交媒体筛查本质上是审查求职者的私人生活。它可以揭示关于年龄、种族、国籍、残疾、性别、宗教等受保护特征的信息，这可能会影响招聘决策。私人页面上被断章取义的图片或评论可能会毁掉一个非常优秀的候选人被录用的机会。这个过程可能给一个候选人带来相对于另一个候选人的不公平优势。它创造了一个不公平的竞争环境，并可能向招聘经理提供可能以负面方式影响其招聘决策的信息。

paragraphs.text: It's hard to ignore social media as a screening tool. While there are things that you shouldn't see, there are some things that can be lawfully considered—making it a valuable source of relevant information too. Using social media screening appropriately can help ensure that you don't hire a toxic employee who will cost you money or stain your company's reputation. Consider the lawful side of this process and you may be able to hire the best employee ever. There is a delicate balance.
paragraphs.translation: 很难忽视社交媒体作为一种筛选工具。虽然有些东西你不应该看到，但有些东西可以被合法考虑——这也使其成为相关信息的宝贵来源。适当使用社交媒体筛查可以帮助确保你不会雇用一个会让你损失金钱或玷污公司声誉的有害员工。考虑到这个过程的合法方面，你可能能够雇用有史以来最好的员工。这存在一个微妙的平衡。

paragraphs.text: Screening job candidates on social media must be done professionally and responsibly. Companies should stipulate that they will never ask for passwords, be consistent, document decisions, consider the source used and be aware that other laws may apply. In light of this it is probably best to look later in the process and ask human resources for help in navigating it. Social media is here to stay. But before using social media to screen job candidates, consulting with management and legal teams beforehand is essential in order to comply with all laws.
paragraphs.translation: 在社交媒体上筛选求职者必须专业且负责任地进行。公司应规定他们绝不会要求密码，保持一致性，记录决策，考虑所使用的来源，并意识到可能适用其他法律。鉴于此，最好在过程中稍后查看，并寻求人力资源部门的帮助来指导。社交媒体将继续存在。但在使用社交媒体筛选求职者之前，事先咨询管理层和法律团队至关重要，以遵守所有法律。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). questions.questionText: What does the author mainly discuss in the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The advantage of using social media in screening job candidates.

options.label: B
options.text: The potentially invasive nature of social media in everyday life.

options.label: C
options.text: Whether the benefits of social media outweigh the drawbacks.

options.label: D
options.text: Whether social media should be used to screen job candidates.

questions.analysis: 这是一道主旨大意题。文章主要讨论了社交媒体在筛选求职者时的使用问题，包括其普遍性、潜在的法律风险和道德问题，以及如何专业和负责任地使用社交媒体信息。因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'The advantage of using social media in screening job candidates'只是文章讨论的一个方面，不是主旨。
wrongOptions.B: 'The potentially invasive nature of social media in everyday life'并未涉及，文章聚焦于招聘过程中的社交媒体使用。
wrongOptions.C: 'Whether the benefits of social media outweigh the drawbacks'文章并未全面讨论社交媒体的利弊，而是侧重于其在招聘中的使用。

questions.questionText: What might happen when social media is used to screen job candidates?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Company reputation might suffer.

options.label: C
options.text: Sensational information might surface.

options.label: D

wrongOptions.B: 'Company reputation might suffer'是可能的后果之一，但文章并未明确提及这一点。
wrongOptions.C: 'Sensational information might surface'并未在文章中提及。
wrongOptions.D: 'Hiring decisions might be complicated'是可能的后果之一，但文章并未明确提及这一点。

questions.questionText: When could online personal information be detrimental to candidates?

options.label: A
options.text: When it is separated from context.

options.label: B
options.text: When it is scrutinised by an employer.

options.label: C
options.text: When it is magnified to a ruinous degree.

options.label: D
options.text: When it is revealed to the human resources.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章提到，社交媒体上的私人信息如果被断章取义可能会对求职者不利，因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 'When it is scrutinised by an employer'文章并未提及雇主审查时信息会有害。
wrongOptions.C: 'When it is magnified to a ruinous degree'并未提及信息被放大到毁灭性的程度。
wrongOptions.D: 'When it is revealed to the human resources'并未提及信息被透露给人力资源部门时会有害。

questions.questionText: How can employers use social media information to their advantage while avoiding unnecessary risks?

options.label: A
options.text: By tipping the delicate balance.

options.label: B
options.text: By using it in a legitimate way.

options.label: C
options.text: By keeping personal information on record.

options.label: D

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章提到，使用社交媒体信息要合法，这样可以避免不必要的风险，因此B选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'By tipping the delicate balance'并未提及打破微妙平衡。
wrongOptions.C: 'By keeping personal information on record'并未提及保留个人信息记录。
wrongOptions.D: 'By separating relevant from irrelevant data'并未提及区分相关和不相关的数据。

questions.questionText: What does the author suggest doing before screening job candidates on social media?

options.label: A
options.text: Hiring professionals to navigate the whole process.

options.label: B
options.text: Anticipating potential risks involved in the process.

options.label: C
options.text: Seeking advice from management and legal experts.

options.label: D
options.text: Stipulating a set of rules for asking specific questions.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章最后一段提到，在社交媒体上筛选求职者之前，最好咨询管理和法律团队，因此C选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Hiring professionals to navigate the whole process'并未提及雇佣专业人员。
wrongOptions.B: 'Anticipating potential risks involved in the process'并未提及预期潜在风险。
wrongOptions.D: 'Stipulating a set of rules for asking specific questions'并未提及制定一套规则来询问特定问题。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: In recent years, the food industry has increased its use of labels. Whether the labels say 'non-GMO (非转基因的)' or 'no sugar', or 'zero carbohydrates', consumers are increasingly demanding more information about what's in their food. One report found that 39 percent of consumers would switch from the brands they currently buy to others that provide clearer, more accurate product information. Food manufacturers are responding to the report with new labels to meet that demand, and they're doing so with an eye towards giving their products an advantage over the competition, and bolstering profits.
paragraphs.translation: 近年来，食品行业增加了标签的使用。无论标签上写着“非转基因”、“无糖”还是“零碳水化合物”，消费者对食品成分信息的需求日益增长。一份报告发现，39%的消费者会从目前购买的品牌转向提供更清晰、更准确产品信息的其他品牌。食品制造商正通过推出新标签来满足这一需求，他们这样做是为了使自己的产品在竞争中占据优势，并增加利润。

paragraphs.text: This strategy makes intuitive sense. If consumers say they want transparency, tell them exactly what is in your product. That is simply supplying a certain demand. But the marketing strategy in response to this consumer demand has gone beyond articulating what is in a product, to labeling what is NOT in the food. These labels are known as "absence claims" labels, and they represent an emerging labeling trend that is detrimental both to the consumers who purchase the products and the industry that supplies them.
paragraphs.translation: 这种策略在直觉上是有道理的。如果消费者要求透明，就告诉他们产品中到底有什么。这仅仅是满足某种需求。但响应这种消费者需求的营销策略已经超出了阐述产品成分的范围，转而标注食品中不含什么。这些标签被称为“缺失声明”标签，它们代表了一种新兴的标签趋势，对购买产品的消费者和供应产品的行业都有害。

paragraphs.text: For example, Hun's put a "non-GMO" label on its canned crushed tomatoes a few years ago—despite the fact that at the time there was no such thing as a GMO tomato on the market. Some dairy companies are using the "non-GMO" label on their milk, despite the fact that all milk is naturally GMO-free, another label that creates unnecessary fear around food.
paragraphs.translation: 例如，Hun's几年前在其罐装碎番茄上贴上了“非转基因”标签——尽管当时市场上根本没有转基因番茄。一些乳制品公司在其牛奶上使用“非转基因”标签，尽管所有牛奶天然就是非转基因的，这又是一个在食品周围制造不必要恐惧的标签。

paragraphs.text: While creating labels that play on consumer fears and misconceptions about their food may give a company a temporary marketing advantage over competing products on the grocery aisle, in the long term this strategy will have just the opposite effect: by injecting fear into the discourse about our food, we run the risk of eroding consumer trust in not just a single product, but the entire food business.
paragraphs.translation: 虽然利用消费者对食品的恐惧和误解来创建标签可能会让公司在杂货店货架上的竞争产品中获得暂时的营销优势，但从长远来看，这种策略会产生相反的效果：通过在食品讨论中注入恐惧，我们不仅可能侵蚀消费者对单一产品的信任，还可能损害整个食品行业的信任。

paragraphs.text: Eventually, it becomes a question in consumers' minds: Were these foods ever safe? By purchasing and consuming these types of products, have I already done some kind of harm to my family or the planet? For food manufacturers, it will mean damaged consumer trust and lower sales for everyone. And this isn't just supposition. A recent study found that absence claims labels can create a stigma around foods even when there is no scientific evidence that they cause harm.
paragraphs.translation: 最终，消费者心中会产生这样的疑问：这些食品曾经安全吗？通过购买和消费这类产品，我已经对我的家人或地球造成了某种伤害吗？对食品制造商来说，这将意味着消费者信任受损和每个人的销售额下降。这不仅仅是假设。最近的一项研究发现，即使没有科学证据表明食品有害，缺失声明标签也会在食品周围制造污名。

paragraphs.text: It's clear that food manufacturers must tread carefully when it comes to using absence claims. In addition to the likely negative long-term impact on sales, this verbal trick sends a message that innovations in farming and food processing are unwelcome, eventually leading to less efficiency, fewer choices for consumers, and ultimately, more costly food products. If we allow this kind of labeling to continue, we will all lose.
paragraphs.translation: 显然，食品制造商在使用缺失声明时必须谨慎行事。除了可能对销售产生长期负面影响外，这种文字技巧传递了一个信息：农业和食品加工的创新不受欢迎，最终导致效率降低、消费者选择减少，以及更昂贵的食品产品。如果我们允许这种标签继续下去，我们都会输。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). questions.questionText: What trend has been observed in a report?

options.label: A
options.text: Food manufacturers' rising awareness of product safety.

options.label: B
options.text: Food manufacturers' changing strategies to bolster profits.

options.label: C
options.text: Consumers' growing demand for eye-catching food labels.

options.label: D
options.text: Consumers' increasing desire for clear product information.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第一段'One report found that 39 percent of consumers would switch from the brands they currently buy to others that provide clearer, more accurate product information'，可以得出消费者越来越渴望清晰的产品信息，因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Food manufacturers' rising awareness of product safety'在文章中没有提及，文章关注的是消费者对产品信息的需求。
wrongOptions.B: 'Food manufacturers' changing strategies to bolster profits'虽然文章提到了制造商为了利润而改变标签策略，但这不是报告观察到的趋势。
wrongOptions.C: 'Consumers' growing demand for eye-catching food labels'文章中提到的是消费者对产品信息的需求，而非对吸引眼球的食品标签的需求。

questions.questionText: What does the author say is manufacturers' new marketing strategy?

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D

wrongOptions.B: 'Articulating the unique nutritional value of their products'文章中没有提到这一点，而是提到了标签中强调产品中没有的元素。
wrongOptions.C: 'Supplying detailed information of their products'虽然文章提到了提供清晰的产品信息，但更强调的是标签中强调产品中没有的元素。
wrongOptions.D: 'Designing transparent labels for their products'文章中没有提到透明标签，而是提到了标签中强调产品中没有的元素。

questions.questionText: What point does the author make about non-GMO labels?

options.label: A
options.text: They are increasingly attracting customers' attention.

options.label: B
options.text: They create lots of trouble for GMO food producers.

options.label: C

options.label: D

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第三段提到'Some dairy companies are using the 'non-GMO' label on their milk, despite the fact that all milk is naturally GMO-free, another label that creates unnecessary fear around food'，说明非转基因标签引起了消费者对食品的不必要恐慌，因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'They are increasingly attracting customers' attention'虽然非转基因标签可能吸引消费者，但文章强调的是它引起的恐慌。
wrongOptions.B: 'They create lots of trouble for GMO food producers'文章中没有提到这一点，而是提到了对消费者的影响。

questions.questionText: What does the author say absence claims labels will do to food manufacturers?

wrongOptions.A: 'Cause changes in their marketing strategies'文章中提到了标签声明对销售和消费者信任的影响，但没有提到营销策略的变化。

wrongOptions.A: 'Take measures to lower the cost of food products'文章中没有提到降低食品成本的问题。
wrongOptions.C: 'Welcome new innovations in food processing'虽然文章提到了食品加工的创新，但并没有建议制造商欢迎这些创新。

questionGroups.sourceText: 井冈山地处湖南江西两省交界处，因其辉煌的革命历史被誉为"中国革命红色摇篮"。1927年10月，毛泽东、朱德等老一辈革命家率领中国工农红军来到这里，开展了艰苦卓绝的斗争，创建了第一个农村革命根据地，点燃了中国革命的星星之火，开辟了"农村包围 (besiege) 城市，武装夺取政权"这一具有中国特色的革命道路，中国革命从这里迈向胜利。井冈山现有 100多处革命旧址，成为一个"没有围墙的革命历史博物馆"，是爱国主义和革命传统教育的重要基地。

answer.modelTranslation: Located at the junction of Hunan and Jiangxi provinces, Jinggangshan is hailed as "the Cradle of the Chinese Revolution" for its glorious revolutionary history. In October 1927, Mao Zedong, Zhu De and other older-generation revolutionaries led the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army here, where they waged an extremely arduous struggle, established the first rural revolutionary base, kindled the spark of the Chinese revolution, and opened up a revolutionary path with Chinese characteristics—"besieging the cities from the countryside and seizing political power by armed force"—from where the Chinese revolution marched on to victory. Today Jinggangshan is home to more than 100 revolutionary sites and has become "a museum of revolutionary history without walls", serving as an important base for patriotic and revolutionary tradition education.
translationNotes: '井冈山地处湖南江西两省交界处'译为'Located at the junction of Hunan and Jiangxi provinces, Jinggangshan...'，用过去分词短语作状语，使句子更紧凑
'被誉为"中国革命红色摇篮"'译为'is hailed as "the Cradle of the Chinese Revolution"'，注意被动语态和专有名词大写
'毛泽东、朱德等老一辈革命家'译为'Mao Zedong, Zhu De and other older-generation revolutionaries'，专有人名按汉语拼音处理
'中国工农红军'译为'the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army'，注意所有格连写
'开展了艰苦卓绝的斗争'译为'waged an extremely arduous struggle'，wage 作动词搭配 struggle/war
'创建了第一个农村革命根据地'译为'established the first rural revolutionary base'，注意 establish 与 base 的搭配
'点燃了中国革命的星星之火'译为'kindled the spark of the Chinese revolution'，保留比喻并使用 kindle
'农村包围城市，武装夺取政权'译为'besieging the cities from the countryside and seizing political power by armed force'，原文括号已给出 besiege 提示
'迈向胜利'译为'marched on to victory'，march on 形象表达持续推进
'没有围墙的革命历史博物馆'译为'a museum of revolutionary history without walls'，保留比喻形象
'爱国主义和革命传统教育的重要基地'译为'an important base for patriotic and revolutionary tradition education'，并列形容词修饰

keyVocabulary.en: the Cradle of the Chinese Revolution
the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army
besiege the cities from the countryside
seize political power by armed force

scoringPoints: 专有名词（井冈山、湖南、江西、毛泽东、朱德等）翻译准确
被动结构'被誉为'翻译得当，使用 be hailed/known as
过去时态贯穿历史叙述，时间状语 In October 1927 与谓语保持一致
并列动词 led / waged / established / kindled / opened up 列举得体，避免重复
比喻表达（'星星之火''没有围墙的革命历史博物馆'）保持形象
复杂修饰短语处理得当，长句拆分合理
